The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

The survey lateral/sibilant outcomes fit the tr-cluster urine family; retroflex muṭ and ordinary mute preserve the same noun, with phonetic details left open. Reviewed comparison: Dotyali mut̚ “urine” (f_hbdj3vaid2wfw). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10066 mārayati gives the mār- kill verb; maral/marla and māryo are ordinary eastern -l and western -y past/infinitive formations. Mār-diyo contains a give light verb and is not assigned as a simple inherited stem. Reviewed comparison: marwari_bagra mārīyɔ “don't kill!, he killed” (f_635k7q3sfgana). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

Eastern -l and western -y inflections can continue the hear stem; sun-lo and ambiguous sunā causative/past forms require local morphology. Reviewed comparison: Dotyali sunyo “listen” (f_652rwzlb2q23m). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
